answer: One defense is latency triangulation: several landmarks measure a new identity's round-trip times and place it on a map. Real agents land at distinct points, while a Sybil farm collapses into one hollow shell — many names sharing one network location — and counts as one. Copper wires set the physics: signals cannot outrun light, so one proxy farm cannot fake far-apart timings. To pass, an attacker must rent machines scattered across regions, one per fake identity, so each extra Sybil pays for distributed hardware, not a cheap copy, and attack cost spirals with size.
